taxonomy:
Below is a practical taxonomy for **grid-based logic puzzles**, with each of your listed games placed under the most fitting “core constraint” category.

## 1) Region / Partition puzzles (divide grid into regions)
- **Shikaku**  
- **Heyawake**  
- **Yosenabe** (region + shading constraints in a similar “region logic” style)

## 2) Path / Loop puzzles (single or multiple continuous loops/paths)
- **Akari** (light rays imply traversable constraints; often treated as ray/loop-like, but see also “ray” below)  
- **Dotchi-Loop**  
- **Masyu**  
- **Yajilin** (paths/rays to shaded numbered endpoints)  
- **Shakashaka**  
- **Slitherlink**  
- **Loop / cycle style:**  
  - **Mid-loop**

## 3) Ray / visibility puzzles (light, beams, line-of-sight)
- **Akari**  
- **Kurodoko** (commonly handled as a ray/visibility + black/white constraint puzzle)  
- **Hashiwokakero** (connected bridges; see also graph/connection, but directionally ray-like paths don’t apply—so keep under “connections”)  
- **Yajilin** (light/detection line-of-sight constraints)

## 4) Bridge / island connection puzzles (graph connectivity on grid)
- **Hashiwokakero**  
- **Satogaeri** (directed/“turning” island connection variant)  
- **Juosan** (connection/flow constraints with islands/cells)

## 5) Drawing single-line puzzles (connective paths without “loop” emphasis)
- **Numberlink**  
- **Nurikabe** (boundary-style connectivity; also a wall/region type—placed here due to wall continuity)  
- **Norinori** (single path traced through cells)

## 6) Fill / polyomino / region-growing puzzles (build shapes on grid)
- **Fillomino**  
- **Evolomino**  
- **Choco Banana**  
- **Double Choco**  
- **Five Cells**  
- **Evolomino**  
- **Nurikabe** (can also be seen as region/walls; keeping it under “walls/regions” below)

## 7) Number placement with grid constraints (classic Sudoku-like)
- **Sudoku**

## 8) “Number in cells” with adjacency rules (local numeric logic)
- **LITS** (line/painted regions + numeric/shape constraints)  
- **Kurotto** (shapes with arithmetic/area-like constraints)  
- **Nansuke** (pairing/inequality-ish rules with numbered cells)

## 9) Wall / barrier puzzles (continuous walls, regions blocked by walls)
- **Nurikabe**  
- **Yosenabe** (often includes “wall-like” constraints via region separation)  

## 10) Painting / color assignment puzzles (black/white shading, multi-state)
- **Hitori**  
- **Kurodoko**  
- **Heyawake** (also partition-like, but specifically black/white island rules)  
- **Nurimeizu** (shaded/colored constraints)  
- **Nurimisaki** (shaded/segmented constraints)  
- **Nuritwin** (shading and twin region interaction)  

## 11) Inequality / relative ordering puzzles (directional constraints)
- **Shakashaka** (nonogram-like removal; but mainly row/column segmentation—kept under “shading/blocking” above if preferred)  
- **Ripple Effect** (propagation order / sequential constraints)  
- **Nagareru** (flow dynamics)  

## 12) Flow / movement / propagation puzzles (simulate movement, diffusion, endpoints)
- **Nagareru**  
- **Ripple Effect**  
- **Usowan** (often treated as propagation/flow from clues)  
- **Suraromu** (movement/constraint propagation style)

## 13) “Topological” or loop-turn constraints (parity/turn/neighbor conditions)
- **Hebi** (snake-like path with turn constraints)  
- **Masyu** (turn/line constraints around beads—also in loop/path category)  
- **Chained Block** (chaining/adjacency constraints with blocks)

## 14) Pairing / balancing puzzles (two types, mirror/twin rules)
- **Nuritwin**  
- **Moon-or-Sun** (binary choice: moon vs sun constraints)

## 15) Grid drawing / partition + border logic (arrows, forced segments)
- **Satogaeri** (also connection/flow),  
- **Makaro** (typically “snake/track” under border/flow constraint styles)

## 16) Line-segment completion / line drawing with endpoints
- **Yajilin** (endpoints + visibility)  
- **LITS** (segment/rules)  
- **Pencils** (pencil/segment connectivity logic)

## 17) Edge/constraint satisfaction with local cell rules (misc. “cell operators”)
- **Tilepaint** (painting/constraints satisfaction)  
- **Sto-stone** (stone movement/stack constraints)  
- **Hebi** (snake/path; placed above)  
- **Sashigane** (clue-based region/connection using “shade lines” style)  
- **Hitori** (already in painting)  

---

- **Suraromu** — Flow/movement

1) refactor the taxonomy into a **smaller set of only 6–8 top-level classes**, or
